title: "Gaussian Process Reading List"
description: "Books, articles, and interactive tools for learning Gaussian processes."

---

This list collects resources for learning Gaussian processes, with an emphasis on intuition, kernels, regression, and visual understanding. The groups follow the original reading notes.

## Books

- *Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning* is the standard mathematical and practical reference for GP models, kernels, and inference [@rasmussen2006]. The full text is available online from the authors.
- *Kernel Methods and Machine Learning* is a useful companion for the broader kernel-methods perspective.
- *Automatic Model Construction with Gaussian Processes* develops compositional approaches for building GP models [@duvenaud2014].
- *Kernel Methods for Machine Learning with Math and Python: 100 Exercises for Building Logic* provides an exercise-oriented route through kernel ideas and implementations.

## Web articles

- [Gaussian Processes for Dummies](https://katbailey.github.io/post/gaussian-processes-for-dummies/) gives an accessible introduction to the main intuition.
- [An introduction to Gaussian Processes](https://ekamperi.github.io/mathematics/2021/03/30/gaussian-process-regression.html) walks through the mathematics of GP regression [@ekamperi2021].
- [Unraveling spectral properties of kernel matrices - I](https://francisbach.com/spectrum-kernel-matrices-i/) and [Part II](https://francisbach.com/spectrum-kernel-matrices-ii/) connect kernel matrices with spectral viewpoints [@bach2023a; @bach2023b].
- [What Is Category Theory, Anyway?](https://www.math3ma.com/blog/what-is-category-theory-anyway) offers an accessible introduction to thinking about mathematical structure and relationships [@bradley2020category].

## Interactive tools

- [Interactive Gaussian Process Visualization](https://www.infinitecuriosity.org/vizgp/) lets you explore how observations change a GP posterior.
- [A Visual Exploration of Gaussian Processes](https://distill.pub/2019/visual-exploration-gaussian-processes/) uses interactive explanations to build intuition for priors, kernels, and posteriors [@google2019].
- [Visualization of Gaussian Process regression](https://smlbook.org/GP/) provides an online visual companion to the GP regression material in *Machine Learning: A Probabilistic Perspective* [@murphy2012].

## Suggested order

1. Start with the visual exploration and introductory articles to develop intuition.
2. Work through the regression demo on this site and compare its prior and posterior plots with the interactive tools.
3. Use *Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning* as the main reference while experimenting with kernels and hyperparameters.
4. Return to the spectral articles and compositional-modeling material once the basic GP workflow is familiar.
